# Authentication

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer

* API Key (cookie_auth)
    - Parameter Name: **connect.sid**, in: cookie.

- HTTP Authentication, scheme: bearer

<h1 id="medusa-storefront-api-auth">Auth</h1>

Auth API routes allow you to manage a customer's authentication.


## Verify the Customer's Email

<a id="opIdPostActor_typeAuth_providerVerificationConfirm"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/auth/customer/emailpass/verification/confirm \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "token": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /auth/customer/emailpass/verification/confirm`

Verifies the customer's email using a token that is typically sent to their email address. This is used to confirm the customer's email during registration or authentication when [email verification is required](https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/commerce-modules/auth/auth-providers/emailpass). You can listen to the `auth.verification_requested` event in a subscriber and send an email to the customer with the verification token.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="verify-the-customers-email-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» token|body|string|true|The verification token sent to the customer's email address.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Discount must be set to dynamic",
  "type": "not_allowed"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Entity with id 1 was not found",
  "type": "not_found"
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "code": "unknown_error",
  "message": "The request conflicted with another request. You may retry the request with the provided Idempotency-Key.",
  "type": "QueryRunnerAlreadyReleasedError"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "code": "invalid_request_error",
  "message": "Discount with code TEST already exists.",
  "type": "duplicate_error"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "code": "api_error",
  "message": "An error occured while hashing password",
  "type": "database_error"
}
```

<h3 id="verify-the-customers-email-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|
|400|Bad Request|Client Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|User is not authorized. Must log in first|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not Found Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|Invalid State Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid Request Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Authenticate Customer

<a id="opIdPostActor_typeAuth_provider"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/auth/customer/emailpass \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{}'
```

`POST /auth/customer/{auth_provider}`

Authenticate a customer and receive the JWT token to be used in the header of subsequent requests.

When used with a third-party provider, such as Google, the request returns a `location` property. You redirect to the specified URL in your storefront to continue authentication with the third-party service.


<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/storefront-development/customers/login#1-using-a-jwt-token">Storefront development: How to login as a customer</a>

## Validate Authentication Callback

<a id="opIdPostActor_typeAuth_providerCallback"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/auth/customer/google/callback \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /auth/customer/{auth_provider}/callback`

This API route is used by your storefront or frontend application when a third-party provider redirects to it after authentication. It validates the authentication with the third-party provider and, if successful, returns an authentication token. All query parameters received from the third-party provider, such as `code`, `state`, and `error`, must be passed as query parameters to this route.
You can decode the JWT token using libraries like [react-jwt](https://www.npmjs.com/package/react-jwt) in the storefront. If the decoded data doesn't  have an `actor_id` property, then you must register the customer using the Create Customer API route passing the token in the request's Authorization header.


<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/storefront-development/customers/third-party-login">Storefront development: Implement third-party (social) login.</a>

<h3 id="validate-authentication-callback-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|auth_provider|path|string|true|The provider used for authentication.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "token": "string"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Discount must be set to dynamic",
  "type": "not_allowed"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Entity with id 1 was not found",
  "type": "not_found"
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "code": "unknown_error",
  "message": "The request conflicted with another request. You may retry the request with the provided Idempotency-Key.",
  "type": "QueryRunnerAlreadyReleasedError"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "code": "invalid_request_error",
  "message": "Discount with code TEST already exists.",
  "type": "duplicate_error"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "code": "api_error",
  "message": "An error occured while hashing password",
  "type": "database_error"
}
```

## Retrieve Registration JWT Token

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/auth/customer/emailpass/register \
```

## Generate Reset Password Token for Customer

<a id="opIdPostActor_typeAuth_providerResetPassword"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/auth/customer/emailpass/reset-password \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "identifier": "customer@gmail.com",
    "metadata": {}
  }'
```

`POST /auth/customer/{auth_provider}/reset-password`

Generate a reset password token for a customer. This API route doesn't reset the customer password or send them the reset instructions in a notification.

Instead, This API route emits the `auth.password_reset` event, passing it the token as a payload. You can listen to that event in a subscriber as explained in [this guide](https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/commerce-modules/auth/reset-password), then send the customer a notification. The notification is sent using a [Notification Module Provider](https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/infrastructure-modules/notification), and it should have a URL that accepts a `token` query parameter, allowing the customer to reset their password from the storefront.


 Use the generated token to update the customer's password using the [Reset Password API route](https://docs.medusajs.com/api/store#auth_postactor_typeauth_providerupdate).


<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/storefront-development/customers/reset-password#1-request-reset-password-page">Storefront development: How to create the request reset password page.</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "identifier": "customer@gmail.com",
  "metadata": {}
}
```

<h3 id="generate-reset-password-token-for-customer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|auth_provider|path|string|true|The provider used for authentication.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» identifier|body|string|true|The customer's identifier for the selected auth provider. For example, for the `emailpass` auth provider, the value is the customer's email.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Optional metadata to include with the reset password token generation request.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Discount must be set to dynamic",
  "type": "not_allowed"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Entity with id 1 was not found",
  "type": "not_found"
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "code": "unknown_error",
  "message": "The request conflicted with another request. You may retry the request with the provided Idempotency-Key.",
  "type": "QueryRunnerAlreadyReleasedError"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "code": "invalid_request_error",
  "message": "Discount with code TEST already exists.",
  "type": "duplicate_error"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "code": "api_error",
  "message": "An error occured while hashing password",
  "type": "database_error"
}
```

<h3 id="generate-reset-password-token-for-customer-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|OK|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Client Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|User is not authorized. Must log in first|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not Found Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|Invalid State Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid Request Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Reset a Customer's Password

<a id="opIdPostActor_typeAuth_providerUpdate"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/auth/customer/emailpass/update \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ACCESS_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{
    "email": "customer@gmail.com",
    "password": "supersecret"
  }'
```

`POST /auth/customer/{auth_provider}/update`

Reset a customer's password using a reset-password token generated with the [Generate Reset Password Token API route](https://docs.medusajs.com/api/store#auth_postactor_typeauth_providerresetpassword). You pass the token as a bearer token in the request's Authorization header.

<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/storefront-development/customers/reset-password#2-reset-password-page">Storefront development: How to create the reset password page.</a>

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/auth/token/refresh \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`POST /auth/token/refresh`

Refresh the authentication token of a customer. This is useful after authenticating a customer with a third-party service to ensure the token holds the new user's details, or when you don't want customers to re-login every day.

<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/storefront-development/customers/third-party-login">Storefront development: Implement third-party (social) login.</a>

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "token": "string"
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Discount must be set to dynamic",
  "type": "not_allowed"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Entity with id 1 was not found",
  "type": "not_found"
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "code": "unknown_error",
  "message": "The request conflicted with another request. You may retry the request with the provided Idempotency-Key.",
  "type": "QueryRunnerAlreadyReleasedError"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "code": "invalid_request_error",
  "message": "Discount with code TEST already exists.",
  "type": "duplicate_error"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "code": "api_error",
  "message": "An error occured while hashing password",
  "type": "database_error"
}
```

<h3 id="refresh-authentication-token-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[AuthResponse](#schemaauthresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Client Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|User is not authorized. Must log in first|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not Found Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|Invalid State Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid Request Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Confirm Customer Verification

<a id="opIdPostVerificationConfirm"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/auth/verification/confirm \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "code": "string",
    "code_provider": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /auth/verification/confirm`

Confirm a verification token of the customer. This API route is used as the last step part of the email verification flow. It can also be used for custom flows, such as phone number verification. Once successfully verified, a customer can complete their registration and log into their account.

<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/storefront-development/customers/verify-account">Storefront guide: Register Customer with Email Verification.</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "code": "string",
  "code_provider": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="confirm-customer-verification-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» code|body|string|true|The token, OTP, or any other code that was sent to the customer for verification.|
|» code_provider|body|string|false|The provider to use for verification. This is optional. When not provided, the default `token` provider is used.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Discount must be set to dynamic",
  "type": "not_allowed"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Entity with id 1 was not found",
  "type": "not_found"
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "code": "unknown_error",
  "message": "The request conflicted with another request. You may retry the request with the provided Idempotency-Key.",
  "type": "QueryRunnerAlreadyReleasedError"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "code": "invalid_request_error",
  "message": "Discount with code TEST already exists.",
  "type": "duplicate_error"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "code": "api_error",
  "message": "An error occured while hashing password",
  "type": "database_error"
}
```

<h3 id="confirm-customer-verification-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|
|400|Bad Request|Client Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|User is not authorized. Must log in first|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not Found Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|Invalid State Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid Request Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Request Customer Verification

<a id="opIdPostVerificationRequest"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/auth/verification/request \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "entity_id": "string",
    "entity_type": "string",
    "code_provider": "string",
    "metadata": {}
  }'
```

`POST /auth/verification/request`

Create a verification request for a customer. This API route is used when a customer logs in, but their email requires verification. It can also be used for custom flows, such as phone number verification. Once successfully requested, a verification code will be generated and an `auth.verification_requested` event will be emitted. You can listen to this event and decide how to deliver the code to the customer.

<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/storefront-development/customers/verify-account">Storefront guide: Register Customer with Email Verification.</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "entity_id": "string",
  "entity_type": "string",
  "code_provider": "string",
  "metadata": {}
}
```

<h3 id="request-customer-verification-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» entity_id|body|string|true|The identifier of the user or customer. For example, an email address.|
|» entity_type|body|string|true|The type of identity being verified. For example, "email" or "phone_number".|
|» code_provider|body|string|true|The provider to use to create the verification token or code. By default, Medusa provides a `token` provider that generates a random token. You can also implement your own provider to generate a code or OTP.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Custom key-value pairs that can be passed to the verification request. This is optional and can be used to store additional information related to the verification request.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Discount must be set to dynamic",
  "type": "not_allowed"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Entity with id 1 was not found",
  "type": "not_found"
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "code": "unknown_error",
  "message": "The request conflicted with another request. You may retry the request with the provided Idempotency-Key.",
  "type": "QueryRunnerAlreadyReleasedError"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "code": "invalid_request_error",
  "message": "Discount with code TEST already exists.",
  "type": "duplicate_error"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "code": "api_error",
  "message": "An error occured while hashing password",
  "type": "database_error"
}
```

<h3 id="request-customer-verification-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|201|Created|OK|None|
|400|Bad Request|Client Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|User is not authorized. Must log in first|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not Found Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|Invalid State Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid Request Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<h1 id="medusa-storefront-api-carts">Carts</h1>

A cart is a virtual shopping bag that customers can use to add items they want to purchase.

A cart is then used to checkout and place an order.

These API routes allow customers to create and manage their cart, and place an order.


<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/storefront-development/cart">How to implement cart functionality in a storefront.</a>

<h3 id="create-cart-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|x-publishable-api-key|header|string|true|Publishable API Key created in the Medusa Admin.|
|x-medusa-locale|header|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|fields|query|string|false|Comma-separated fields that should be included in the returned data. if a field is prefixed with `+` it will be added to the default fields, using `-` will remove it from the default fields. without prefix it will replace the entire default fields.|
|locale|query|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» region_id|body|string|false|The ID of the cart's region. This affects the prices and currency of the cart.|
|» shipping_address|body|[StoreCartAddress](#schemastorecartaddress)|false|The address's details.|
|» billing_address|body|[StoreCartAddress](#schemastorecartaddress)|false|The address's details.|
|» email|body|string(email)|false|The email of the cart's customer.|
|» currency_code|body|string|false|The cart's currency code. If not provided, the region's currency is used. This affects prices in the cart, as well.|
|» items|body|[[StoreCartLineItem](#schemastorecartlineitem)]|false|The cart's items.|
|» sales_channel_id|body|string|false|The ID of the sales channel that cart is created in. If not provided, the store's default sales channel is associated with the cart instead.<br><br>A product's availability in a sales channel only filters the products you retrieve. Medusa doesn't reject a variant added to the cart when its product isn't available in the cart's sales channel. Refer to the guide in the external documentation to learn how to enforce that validation.<br>|
|» metadata|body|object|false|The cart's metadata, can hold custom key-value pairs.|
|» additional_data|body|object|false|Pass additional custom data to the API route. This data is passed to the underlying workflow under the `additional_data` parameter.|

<h3 id="create-cart-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[StoreCartResponse](#schemastorecartresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Client Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|User is not authorized. Must log in first|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not Found Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|Invalid State Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid Request Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get a Cart

<a id="opIdGetCartsId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/store/carts/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'x-publishable-api-key: string'
```

`GET /store/carts/{id}`

Retrieve a cart by its ID. You can expand the cart's relations or select the fields that should be returned.

<h3 id="get-a-cart-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The cart's ID.|
|x-publishable-api-key|header|string|true|Publishable API Key created in the Medusa Admin.|
|x-medusa-locale|header|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|fields|query|string|false|Comma-separated fields that should be included in the returned data. if a field is prefixed with `+` it will be added to the default fields, using `-` will remove it from the default fields. without prefix it will replace the entire default fields.|
|locale|query|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|

## Update a Cart

<a id="opIdPostCartsId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/store/carts/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'x-publishable-api-key: string' \
  -d '{
    "region_id": "string",
    "customer_id": "string",
    "sales_channel_id": "string",
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "currency_code": "usd",
    "shipping_address_id": "string",
    "billing_address_id": "string",
    "billing_address": {
      "customer_id": "string",
      "company": "string",
      "first_name": "string",
      "last_name": "string",
      "address_1": "string",
      "address_2": "string",
      "city": "string",
      "country_code": "us",
      "province": "us-ca",
      "postal_code": "string",
      "phone": "string",
      "metadata": {}
    },
    "shipping_address": {
      "customer_id": "string",
      "company": "string",
      "first_name": "string",
      "last_name": "string",
      "address_1": "string",
      "address_2": "string",
      "city": "string",
      "country_code": "us",
      "province": "us-ca",
      "postal_code": "string",
      "phone": "string",
      "metadata": {}
    },
    "metadata": {},
    "additional_data": {}
  }'
```

`POST /store/carts/{id}`

Update a cart's details. This unsets the payment methods chosen before, and the customer would have to choose them again. Also, if the customer has chosen a shipping method whose option isn't valid for the cart's shipping address anymore, the shipping method will be unset. For example, if the shipping option is valid only in the US geo zone, and the shipping address's country code is `DE`, the shipping method will be unset.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "region_id": "string",
  "customer_id": "string",
  "sales_channel_id": "string",
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "currency_code": "usd",
  "shipping_address_id": "string",
  "billing_address_id": "string",
  "billing_address": {
    "customer_id": "string",
    "company": "string",
    "first_name": "string",
    "last_name": "string",
    "address_1": "string",
    "address_2": "string",
    "city": "string",
    "country_code": "us",
    "province": "us-ca",
    "postal_code": "string",
    "phone": "string",
    "metadata": {}
  },
  "shipping_address": {
    "customer_id": "string",
    "company": "string",
    "first_name": "string",
    "last_name": "string",
    "address_1": "string",
    "address_2": "string",
    "city": "string",
    "country_code": "us",
    "province": "us-ca",
    "postal_code": "string",
    "phone": "string",
    "metadata": {}
  },
  "metadata": {},
  "additional_data": {}
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-cart-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The cart's ID.|
|x-publishable-api-key|header|string|true|Publishable API Key created in the Medusa Admin.|
|x-medusa-locale|header|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|fields|query|string|false|Comma-separated fields that should be included in the returned data. if a field is prefixed with `+` it will be added to the default fields, using `-` will remove it from the default fields. without prefix it will replace the entire default fields.|
|locale|query|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» region_id|body|string|false|The ID of the associated region. This can affect the prices and currency code of the cart.|
|» customer_id|body|string|false|The ID of the customer that the cart belongs to.|
|» sales_channel_id|body|string|false|The ID of the associated sales channel.<br><br>A product's availability in a sales channel only filters the products you retrieve. Medusa doesn't reject a variant added to the cart when its product isn't available in the cart's sales channel. Refer to the guide in the external documentation to learn how to enforce that validation.<br>|
|» email|body|string(email)|false|The email of the customer that the cart belongs to.|
|» currency_code|body|string|false|The cart's currency code.|
|» shipping_address_id|body|string|false|The ID of the cart's shipping address.|
|» billing_address_id|body|string|false|The ID of the cart's billing address.|
|» billing_address|body|[CreateAddress](#schemacreateaddress) \| [UpdateAddress](#schemaupdateaddress)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[CreateAddress](#schemacreateaddress)|false|The address to create.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[UpdateAddress](#schemaupdateaddress)|false|The details to update in the address.|
|» shipping_address|body|[CreateAddress](#schemacreateaddress) \| [UpdateAddress](#schemaupdateaddress)|false|none|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[CreateAddress](#schemacreateaddress)|false|The address to create.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[UpdateAddress](#schemaupdateaddress)|false|The details to update in the address.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|The cart's metadata, ca hold custom key-value pairs.|
|» additional_data|body|object|false|Pass additional custom data to the API route. This data is passed to the underlying workflow under the `additional_data` parameter.|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Client Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

|404|Not Found|Not Found Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|Invalid State Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid Request Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="update-a-cart-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|cart|[StoreCart](#schemastorecart)|true|none|The cart's details.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Complete Cart

<a id="opIdPostCartsIdComplete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/store/carts/string/complete \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'x-publishable-api-key: string'
```

`POST /store/carts/{id}/complete`

Complete a cart and place an order.

<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/storefront-development/checkout/complete-cart">Storefront guide: How to implement cart completion during checkout.</a>

<h3 id="complete-cart-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The cart's ID.|
|x-publishable-api-key|header|string|true|Publishable API Key created in the Medusa Admin.|
|x-medusa-locale|header|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|fields|query|string|false|Comma-separated fields that should be included in the returned data. if a field is prefixed with `+` it will be added to the default fields, using `-` will remove it from the default fields. without prefix it will replace the entire default fields.|
|locale|query|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|

<h3 id="complete-cart-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Client Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|User is not authorized. Must log in first|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not Found Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|Invalid State Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid Request Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="complete-cart-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|The created order's details.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the returned object. In this case, the order is returned because the cart was completed successfully.|
|order|[StoreOrder](#schemastoreorder)|true|none|The order's details.|
|*oneOf*|object|false|none|The details of why the cart completion failed.|
|type|string|true|none|The type of the returned object. In this case, the cart is returned because an error has occurred.|
|cart|[StoreCart](#schemastorecart)|true|none|The cart's details.|
|error|object|true|none|The error's details.|
|» message|string|true|none|The error's message.|
|» name|string|true|none|The error's name.|
|» type|string|true|none|The error's type. Can be a [MedusaError type](https://docs.medusajs.com/learn/fundamentals/api-routes/errors#medusaerror-types) or `payment_authorization_error` or `payment_requires_more_error` for payment-related errors.<br>|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Change Cart's Customer to Logged-in Customer

<a id="opIdPostCartsIdCustomer"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/store/carts/string/customer \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'x-publishable-api-key: string' \
  -H "Cookie: connect.sid=${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "additional_data": {}
  }'
```

`POST /store/carts/{id}/customer`

Change the cart's customer to the currently logged-in customer. This is useful when you create the cart for a guest customer, then they log in with their account.

<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/storefront-development/cart/update#set-carts-customer">Storefront guide: How to set the cart's customer.</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "additional_data": {}
}
```

<h3 id="change-carts-customer-to-logged-in-customer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The cart's ID.|
|x-publishable-api-key|header|string|true|Publishable API Key created in the Medusa Admin.|
|x-medusa-locale|header|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|fields|query|string|false|Comma-separated fields that should be included in the returned data.<br>if a field is prefixed with `+` it will be added to the default fields, using `-` will remove it from the default fields.<br>without prefix it will replace the entire default fields.|
|locale|query|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» additional_data|body|object|false|Pass additional custom data to the API route. This data is passed to the underlying workflow under the `additional_data` parameter.|

<h3 id="change-carts-customer-to-logged-in-customer-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[StoreCartResponse](#schemastorecartresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Client Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|User is not authorized. Must log in first|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not Found Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|Invalid State Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid Request Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
cookie_auth, jwt_token
</aside>

## Add Gift Card to Cart

<a id="opIdPostCartsIdGiftCards"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/store/carts/string/gift-cards \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'x-publishable-api-key: string' \
  -d '{
    "code": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /store/carts/{id}/gift-cards`

Add a Gift Card to a cart

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "code": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="add-gift-card-to-cart-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The cart's ID.|
|x-publishable-api-key|header|string|true|Publishable API Key created in the Medusa Admin.|
|x-medusa-locale|header|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|locale|query|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|body|body|[StoreAddGiftCardToCart](#schemastoreaddgiftcardtocart)|false|none|
|» code|body|string|true|The gift card's code.|

|---|---|---|---|

</aside>

## Remove Gift Card from Cart

<a id="opIdDeleteCartsIdGiftCards"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/store/carts/string/gift-cards \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'x-publishable-api-key: string' \
  -d '{
    "code": "string"
  }'
```

`DELETE /store/carts/{id}/gift-cards`

Remove a Gift Card from a cart.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "code": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="remove-gift-card-from-cart-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The cart's ID.|
|x-publishable-api-key|header|string|true|Publishable API Key created in the Medusa Admin.|
|x-medusa-locale|header|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|locale|query|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|body|body|[StoreRemoveGiftCardFromCart](#schemastoreremovegiftcardfromcart)|false|none|
|» code|body|string|true|The gift card code to remove from the cart.|

|---|---|---|---|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Add Line Item to Cart

<a id="opIdPostCartsIdLineItems"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/store/carts/string/line-items \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'x-publishable-api-key: string' \
  -d '{
    "variant_id": "string",
    "quantity": 0,
    "metadata": {},
    "additional_data": {}
  }'
```

`POST /store/carts/{id}/line-items`

Add a product variant as a line item in the cart.

<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/storefront-development/cart/manage-items#add-product-variant-to-cart">Storefront guide: How to add a product variant to the cart.</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "variant_id": "string",
  "quantity": 0,
  "metadata": {},
  "additional_data": {}
}
```

<h3 id="add-line-item-to-cart-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The cart's ID.|
|x-publishable-api-key|header|string|true|Publishable API Key created in the Medusa Admin.|
|x-medusa-locale|header|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|fields|query|string|false|Comma-separated fields that should be included in the returned data. if a field is prefixed with `+` it will be added to the default fields, using `-` will remove it from the default fields. without prefix it will replace the entire default fields.|
|locale|query|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» variant_id|body|string|true|The ID of the product variant to add as a line item.|
|» quantity|body|number|true|The item's quantity.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|The item's metadata, can hold custom key-value pairs.|
|» additional_data|body|object|false|Pass additional custom data to the API route. This data is passed to the underlying workflow under the `additional_data` parameter.|

|200|OK|OK|[StoreCartResponse](#schemastorecartresponse)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Update a Line Item in a Cart

<a id="opIdPostCartsIdLineItemsLine_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/store/carts/string/line-items/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'x-publishable-api-key: string' \
  -d '{
    "quantity": 0,
    "metadata": {},
    "additional_data": {}
  }'
```

`POST /store/carts/{id}/line-items/{line_id}`

Update a line item's details in the cart.

<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/storefront-development/cart/manage-items#update-line-item-in-cart">Storefront guide: How to update a cart's line item.</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "quantity": 0,
  "metadata": {},
  "additional_data": {}
}
```

<h3 id="update-a-line-item-in-a-cart-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The cart's ID.|
|line_id|path|string|true|The line item's ID.|
|x-publishable-api-key|header|string|true|Publishable API Key created in the Medusa Admin.|
|x-medusa-locale|header|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|fields|query|string|false|Comma-separated fields that should be included in the returned data. if a field is prefixed with `+` it will be added to the default fields, using `-` will remove it from the default fields. without prefix it will replace the entire default fields.|
|locale|query|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» quantity|body|number|true|The item's quantity.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|The item's metadata, can hold custom key-value pairs.|
|» additional_data|body|object|false|Pass additional custom data to the API route. This data is passed to the underlying workflow under the `additional_data` parameter.|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[StoreCartResponse](#schemastorecartresponse)|
|400|Bad Request|Client Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|User is not authorized. Must log in first|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not Found Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid Request Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Remove Line Item from Cart

<a id="opIdDeleteCartsIdLineItemsLine_id"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/store/carts/string/line-items/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'x-publishable-api-key: string'
```

`DELETE /store/carts/{id}/line-items/{line_id}`

Remove a line item from a cart.

<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/storefront-development/cart/manage-items#remove-line-item-from-cart">Storefront guide: How to remove line item from cart.</a>

<h3 id="remove-line-item-from-cart-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The cart's ID.|
|line_id|path|string|true|The line item's ID.|
|x-publishable-api-key|header|string|true|Publishable API Key created in the Medusa Admin.|
|x-medusa-locale|header|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|fields|query|string|false|Comma-separated fields that should be included in the returned data. if a field is prefixed with `+` it will be added to the default fields, using `-` will remove it from the default fields. without prefix it will replace the entire default fields.|
|locale|query|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Client Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|User is not authorized. Must log in first|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not Found Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|Invalid State Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid Request Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="remove-line-item-from-cart-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|string|true|none|The ID of the deleted line item.|
|object|string|true|none|The name of the deleted object.|
|deleted|boolean|true|none|Whether the item was deleted.|
|parent|[StoreCart](#schemastorecart)|false|none|The cart that the item belonged to.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Add Promotions to Cart

<a id="opIdPostCartsIdPromotions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/store/carts/string/promotions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'x-publishable-api-key: string' \
  -d '{
    "promo_codes": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`POST /store/carts/{id}/promotions`

Add a list of promotions to a cart.

<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/storefront-development/cart/manage-promotions#add-promotion-to-cart">Storefront guide: How to add a promotion to cart.</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "promo_codes": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="add-promotions-to-cart-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The cart's ID.|
|x-publishable-api-key|header|string|true|Publishable API Key created in the Medusa Admin.|
|x-medusa-locale|header|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|fields|query|string|false|Comma-separated fields that should be included in the returned data. if a field is prefixed with `+` it will be added to the default fields, using `-` will remove it from the default fields. without prefix it will replace the entire default fields.|
|locale|query|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|body|body|[StoreCartAddPromotion](#schemastorecartaddpromotion)|false|none|
|» promo_codes|body|[string]|true|Promotion codes to add to the cart.|

</aside>

## Remove Promotions from Cart

<a id="opIdDeleteCartsIdPromotions"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/store/carts/string/promotions \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'x-publishable-api-key: string' \
  -d '{
    "promo_codes": [
      "string"
    ]
  }'
```

`DELETE /store/carts/{id}/promotions`

Remove a list of promotions from a cart.

<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/storefront-development/cart/manage-promotions#remove-promotion-from-cart">Storefront guide: How to remove a promotion from cart.</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "promo_codes": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="remove-promotions-from-cart-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The cart's ID.|
|x-publishable-api-key|header|string|true|Publishable API Key created in the Medusa Admin.|
|x-medusa-locale|header|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|fields|query|string|false|Comma-separated fields that should be included in the returned data. if a field is prefixed with `+` it will be added to the default fields, using `-` will remove it from the default fields. without prefix it will replace the entire default fields.|
|locale|query|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|body|body|[StoreCartRemovePromotion](#schemastorecartremovepromotion)|false|none|
|» promo_codes|body|[string]|true|The promotion code to remove from the cart.|

## Add Shipping Method to Cart

<a id="opIdPostCartsIdShippingMethods"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/store/carts/string/shipping-methods \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'x-publishable-api-key: string' \
  -d '{
    "option_id": "string",
    "data": {},
    "additional_data": {}
  }'
```

`POST /store/carts/{id}/shipping-methods`

Add a shipping method to a cart. Use this API route when the customer chooses their preferred shipping option.

If the chosen shipping option's `price_type` is `calculated`, its price is computed by the associated fulfillment provider when it's added to the cart. If the provider fails to calculate the price, this route returns an error.


<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/storefront-development/checkout/shipping">Storefront guide: How to implement shipping during checkout.</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "option_id": "string",
  "data": {},
  "additional_data": {}
}
```

<h3 id="add-shipping-method-to-cart-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The cart's ID.|
|x-publishable-api-key|header|string|true|Publishable API Key created in the Medusa Admin.|
|x-medusa-locale|header|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|locale|query|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|fields|query|string|false|Comma-separated fields that should be included in the returned data. If a field is prefixed with `+` it will be added to the default fields, using `-` will remove it from the default fields. Without prefix it will replace the entire default fields.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» option_id|body|string|true|The ID of the shipping option to add to the cart.|
|» data|body|object|false|Any additional data relevant for the third-party fulfillment provider to process the shipment.|
|» additional_data|body|object|false|Pass additional custom data to the API route. This data is passed to the underlying workflow under the `additional_data` parameter.|
|» *oneOf*|body|object|false|none|
|» additional_data|body|object|false|Pass additional custom data to the API route. This data is passed to the underlying workflow under the `additional_data` parameter.|

## Add Store Credit to Cart

<a id="opIdPostCartsIdStoreCredits"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/store/carts/string/store-credits \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'x-publishable-api-key: string' \
  -d '{
    "amount": 0
  }'
```

`POST /store/carts/{id}/store-credits`

Add a Store Credit to a cart

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "amount": 0
}
```

<h3 id="add-store-credit-to-cart-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The cart's ID.|
|x-publishable-api-key|header|string|true|Publishable API Key created in the Medusa Admin.|
|x-medusa-locale|header|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|locale|query|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|body|body|[StoreAddStoreCreditsToCart](#schemastoreaddstorecreditstocart)|false|none|
|» amount|body|number|true|The amount of store credits to add to the cart.|

## Calculate Cart Taxes

<a id="opIdPostCartsIdTaxes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/store/carts/string/taxes \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'x-publishable-api-key: string'
```

`POST /store/carts/{id}/taxes`

Calculate the cart's tax lines and amounts.

Medusa recalculates a cart's tax lines automatically on cart changes when the cart's region has `automatic_taxes` enabled, so you typically don't need to use this route. Use this route to force a recalculation, such as when `automatic_taxes` is disabled, which also triggers a fresh calculation from your third-party tax provider, if you use one.

<h3 id="calculate-cart-taxes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The cart's ID.|
|x-publishable-api-key|header|string|true|Publishable API Key created in the Medusa Admin.|
|x-medusa-locale|header|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|locale|query|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|fields|query|string|false|Comma-separated fields that should be included in the returned data. If a field is prefixed with `+` it will be added to the default fields, using `-` will remove it from the default fields. Without prefix it will replace the entire default fields.|

<h1 id="medusa-storefront-api-collections">Collections</h1>

A product collection organizes products into a collection for marketing purposes. For example, a summer collection.

These API routes allow customers to browse collections and their products.


<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/storefront-development/products/collections/list">How to list product collections in a storefront.</a>

## List Collections

<a id="opIdGetCollections"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/store/collections \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'x-publishable-api-key: string'
```

`GET /store/collections`

Retrieve a list of collections. The collections can be filtered by fields such as `handle`. The collections can also be sorted or paginated.

<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/storefront-development/products/collections/list">Storefront guide: How to retrieve a list of collections.</a>

<h3 id="list-collections-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|x-publishable-api-key|header|string|true|Publishable API Key created in the Medusa Admin.|
|x-medusa-locale|header|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|fields|query|string|false|Comma-separated fields that should be included in the returned data. if a field is prefixed with `+` it will be added to the default fields, using `-` will remove it from the default fields. without prefix it will replace the entire default fields.|
|offset|query|number|false|The number of items to skip when retrieving a list.|
|limit|query|number|false|Limit the number of items returned in the list.|
|order|query|string|false|The field to sort the data by. By default, the sort order is ascending. To change the order to descending, prefix the field name with `-`.|
|title|query|string \| [string]|false|none|
|created_at|query|object|false|Filter by the collection's creation date.|
|updated_at|query|object|false|Filter by the collection's update date.|
|handle|query|string \| [string]|false|none|
|q|query|string|false|Search term to filter the collection's searchable properties.|
|$and|query|[object]|false|Join query parameters with an AND condition. Each object's content is the same type as the expected query parameters.|
|$or|query|[object]|false|Join query parameters with an OR condition. Each object's content is the same type as the expected query parameters.|
|with_deleted|query|boolean|false|Whether to include deleted records in the result.|
|id|query|string \| [string]|false|none|
|locale|query|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|external_id|query|string \| [string]|false|none|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "limit": 0,
  "offset": 0,
  "count": 0,
  "collections": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "title": "string",
      "handle": "string",
      "created_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "updated_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "deleted_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "products": [
        {}
      ],
      "metadata": {},
      "external_id": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Discount must be set to dynamic",
  "type": "not_allowed"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Entity with id 1 was not found",
  "type": "not_found"
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "code": "unknown_error",
  "message": "The request conflicted with another request. You may retry the request with the provided Idempotency-Key.",
  "type": "QueryRunnerAlreadyReleasedError"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "code": "invalid_request_error",
  "message": "Discount with code TEST already exists.",
  "type": "duplicate_error"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "code": "api_error",
  "message": "An error occured while hashing password",
  "type": "database_error"
}
```

<h3 id="list-collections-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Client Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|User is not authorized. Must log in first|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not Found Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|Invalid State Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid Request Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="list-collections-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|number|true|none|The maximum number of items returned.|
|offset|number|true|none|The number of items skipped before retrieving the returned items.|
|count|number|true|none|The total number of items.|
|collections|[[StoreCollection](#schemastorecollection)]|true|none|The collection's collections.|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Get a Collection

<a id="opIdGetCollectionsId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/store/collections/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'x-publishable-api-key: string'
```

`GET /store/collections/{id}`

Retrieve a collection by its ID. You can expand the collection's relations or select the fields that should be returned.

<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/storefront-development/products/collections/retrieve">Storefront guide: How to retrieve a collection.</a>

<h3 id="get-a-collection-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|x-publishable-api-key|header|string|true|Publishable API Key created in the Medusa Admin.|
|x-medusa-locale|header|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|fields|query|string|false|Comma-separated fields that should be included in the returned data. if a field is prefixed with `+` it will be added to the default fields, using `-` will remove it from the default fields. without prefix it will replace the entire default fields.|
|locale|query|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|

```json
    "deleted_at": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",

}
```

<h1 id="medusa-storefront-api-currencies">Currencies</h1>

A store has multiple currencies, and product prices can be different for each currency.

When retrieving product variant prices, you specify either the ID of a region or a currency that the customer selected.

These API routes allow customers to browse currencies.


<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/storefront-development/products/price">How to retrieve product variant prices in a storefront.</a>

## List Currencies

<a id="opIdGetCurrencies"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/store/currencies \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'x-publishable-api-key: string'
```

`GET /store/currencies`

Retrieve a list of currencies. The currencies can be filtered by fields such as `code`. The currencies can also be sorted or paginated.

<h3 id="list-currencies-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|x-publishable-api-key|header|string|true|Publishable API Key created in the Medusa Admin.|
|x-medusa-locale|header|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|fields|query|string|false|Comma-separated fields that should be included in the returned data. if a field is prefixed with `+` it will be added to the default fields, using `-` will remove it from the default fields. without prefix it will replace the entire default fields.|
|offset|query|number|false|The number of items to skip when retrieving a list.|
|limit|query|number|false|Limit the number of items returned in the list.|
|order|query|string|false|The field to sort the data by. By default, the sort order is ascending. To change the order to descending, prefix the field name with `-`.|
|q|query|string|false|Search term to filter the currency's searchable properties.|
|code|query|string \| [string]|false|none|
|$and|query|[object]|false|Join query parameters with an AND condition. Each object's content is the same type as the expected query parameters.|
|$or|query|[object]|false|Join query parameters with an OR condition. Each object's content is the same type as the expected query parameters.|
|with_deleted|query|boolean|false|Whether to include deleted records in the result.|
|locale|query|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|

> Example responses

```json
  "limit": 0,
  "offset": 0,

    {
```

<h1 id="medusa-storefront-api-customers">Customers</h1>

Customers can place orders as guest customers or register.

When a customer registers, they can manage their profile, save addresses for later usage, and more.

These API routes allow customers to create and manage their accounts.


<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/storefront-development/customers">How to implement customer account functionalities in a storefront.</a>

## Register Customer

<a id="opIdPostCustomers"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/store/customers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'x-publishable-api-key: string' \
  -H "Cookie: connect.sid=${API_KEY}" \
  -d '{
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "company_name": "string",
    "first_name": "string",
    "last_name": "string",
    "phone": "string",
    "metadata": {}
  }'
```

`POST /store/customers`

Register a customer. Use the `/auth/customer/emailpass/register` API route first to retrieve the registration token and pass it in the header of the request.

<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/storefront-development/customers/register">Storefront guide: How to register a customer.</a>

```json
  "last_name": "string",

  "metadata": {}
```

`GET /store/customers/me/addresses`

Retrieve the addresses of the logged-in customer. The addresses can be filtered by fields such as `country_code`. The addresses can also be sorted or paginated.

<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/storefront-development/customers/addresses#list-customer-addresses">Storefront guide: How to retrieve the logged-in customer's addresses.</a>

<h3 id="list-customers-addresses-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|x-publishable-api-key|header|string|true|Publishable API Key created in the Medusa Admin.|
|x-medusa-locale|header|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|city|query|string \| [string]|false|Filter by the address's city.|
|postal_code|query|string \| [string]|false|Filter by the address's postal code.|
|country_code|query|string \| [string]|false|Filter by the address's country code.|
|q|query|string|false|Search term to filter the address's searchable properties.|
|$and|query|[object]|false|Join query parameters with an AND condition. Each object's content is the same type as the expected query parameters.|
|$or|query|[object]|false|Join query parameters with an OR condition. Each object's content is the same type as the expected query parameters.|
|locale|query|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|limit|query|number|false|Limit the number of items returned in the list.|
|offset|query|number|false|The number of items to skip when retrieving a list.|
|order|query|string|false|The field to sort the data by. By default, the sort order is ascending. To change the order to descending, prefix the field name with `-`.|
|with_deleted|query|boolean|false|The customer's with deleted.|
|fields|query|string|false|Comma-separated fields that should be included in the returned data. If a field is prefixed with `+` it will be added to the default fields, using `-` will remove it from the default fields. Without prefix it will replace the entire default fields.|

<h1 id="medusa-storefront-api-gift-cards">Gift Cards</h1>

A gift card is a prepaid card that customers can use to purchase products in the store.
Customers can purchase gift cards for themselves or others, and then use them to pay for their orders.
These API routes allow logged-in customers to create and manage their gift cards.
<Note>
Gift Cards are available through the [Loyalty Plugin](https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/commerce-modules/loyalty).
</Note>


## Get a Gift Card

```bash
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'x-publishable-api-key: string'
```

<h1 id="medusa-storefront-api-locales">Locales</h1>

A locale is a language that content is translated into for customers to view in a storefront.
Medusa installs locales by default. These API routes allow you to retrieve supported locales in the store.


<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/commerce-modules/translation/concepts">Learn more about locales and translations.</a>

<h1 id="medusa-storefront-api-multi-factor-authentication-mfa-factors">Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Factors</h1>

Multi-factor authentication (MFA) factors are additional ways to verify a customer's identity during login, in addition to their password. Examples of MFA factors include authenticator apps, SMS messages, and email.
These API routes allow customers to manage their MFA factors, such as enabling an authenticator app or generating recovery codes.


<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/commerce-modules/auth/mfa">Learn more about MFA in Medusa</a>

## Verify a Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Challenge

<a id="opIdPostMfaChallengesIdVerify"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/auth/mfa/challenges/string/verify \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "method": "string",
    "code": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /auth/mfa/challenges/{id}/verify`

Verify a multi-factor authentication (MFA) challenge issued during login. On success, this
completes the authentication flow and returns a JWT token that can be used to authenticate
subsequent requests.


<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/commerce-modules/auth/mfa">Learn more about MFA in Medusa</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "method": "string",
  "code": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="verify-a-multi-factor-authentication-mfa-challenge-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The MFA challenge's ID.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» method|body|string|true|The MFA method used to verify the challenge (for example, `totp` or `recovery-code`).|
|» code|body|string|true|The verification code generated by the chosen MFA method.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Discount must be set to dynamic",
  "type": "not_allowed"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Entity with id 1 was not found",
  "type": "not_found"
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "code": "unknown_error",
  "message": "The request conflicted with another request. You may retry the request with the provided Idempotency-Key.",
  "type": "QueryRunnerAlreadyReleasedError"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "code": "invalid_request_error",
  "message": "Discount with code TEST already exists.",
  "type": "duplicate_error"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "code": "api_error",
  "message": "An error occured while hashing password",
  "type": "database_error"
}
```

<h3 id="verify-a-multi-factor-authentication-mfa-challenge-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|
|400|Bad Request|Client Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|User is not authorized. Must log in first|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not Found Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|Invalid State Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid Request Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## Start Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Factor Enrollment

<a id="opIdPostMfaFactors"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/auth/mfa/factors \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "provider": "string",
    "label": "string",
    "issuer": "string",
    "metadata": {}
  }'
```

`POST /auth/mfa/factors`

Start the enrollment of a new multi-factor authentication (MFA) factor for the authenticated
user. The response contains the factor along with provider-specific setup data (such as a
secret and an `otpauth_url` for TOTP) that can be used to display a QR code. The factor must
then be verified via the verify endpoint before it can be used.


<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/commerce-modules/auth/mfa">Learn more about MFA in Medusa</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "provider": "string",
  "label": "string",
  "issuer": "string",
  "metadata": {}
}
```

<h3 id="start-multi-factor-authentication-mfa-factor-enrollment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» provider|body|string|true|The ID of the MFA provider to enroll the factor with (for example, `totp`).|
|» label|body|string|false|A human-readable label to identify the factor (for example, the name of the authenticator app or device).|
|» issuer|body|string|false|The issuer name shown in authenticator apps for this factor. Defaults to the application name when omitted.|
|» metadata|body|object|false|Additional provider-specific data to associate with the factor.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Discount must be set to dynamic",
  "type": "not_allowed"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Entity with id 1 was not found",
  "type": "not_found"
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "code": "unknown_error",
  "message": "The request conflicted with another request. You may retry the request with the provided Idempotency-Key.",
  "type": "QueryRunnerAlreadyReleasedError"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "code": "invalid_request_error",
  "message": "Discount with code TEST already exists.",
  "type": "duplicate_error"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "code": "api_error",
  "message": "An error occured while hashing password",
  "type": "database_error"
}
```

<h3 id="start-multi-factor-authentication-mfa-factor-enrollment-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|None|
|400|Bad Request|Client Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|User is not authorized. Must log in first|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not Found Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|Invalid State Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid Request Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

## Disable a Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Factor

<a id="opIdDeleteMfaFactorsId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/auth/mfa/factors/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "method": "string",
    "code": "string"
  }'
```

`DELETE /auth/mfa/factors/{id}`

Disable a multi-factor authentication (MFA) factor for the authenticated user. Once disabled,
the factor can no longer be used to verify MFA challenges. When disabling a recovery-code
factor, a valid recovery code must be provided in the request body.


> Body parameter

```json
{
  "method": "string",
  "code": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="disable-a-multi-factor-authentication-mfa-factor-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The MFA factor's ID.|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» method|body|string|false|The MFA method used to authorize disabling the factor (for example, `recovery-code`).|
|» code|body|string|false|The verification code associated with the provided `method`, used to confirm the disable action.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Discount must be set to dynamic",
  "type": "not_allowed"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Entity with id 1 was not found",
  "type": "not_found"
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{
  "code": "unknown_error",
  "message": "The request conflicted with another request. You may retry the request with the provided Idempotency-Key.",
  "type": "QueryRunnerAlreadyReleasedError"
}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "code": "invalid_request_error",
  "message": "Discount with code TEST already exists.",
  "type": "duplicate_error"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "code": "api_error",
  "message": "An error occured while hashing password",
  "type": "database_error"
}
```

<h3 id="disable-a-multi-factor-authentication-mfa-factor-responses">Responses</h3>

<a id="opIdPostMfaFactorsIdVerify"></a>

```bash
  -X POST \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \

    "code": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /auth/mfa/factors/{id}/verify`

Verify a pending multi-factor authentication (MFA) factor by submitting a code generated from

challenges during login.

|body|body|object|false|none|

## Generate Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Recovery Codes

<a id="opIdPostMfaRecoveryCodes"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/auth/mfa/recovery-codes \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "count": 0
  }'
```

`POST /auth/mfa/recovery-codes`

Generate a new set of single-use recovery codes for the authenticated user. Recovery codes can
be used to verify MFA challenges when the user does not have access to their primary MFA
factor. Generating new codes replaces any previously issued codes, so they should be stored in
a safe place. At least one enabled MFA factor is required to generate recovery codes.


<a href="https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/commerce-modules/auth/mfa">Learn more about MFA in Medusa</a>

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "count": 0
}
```

<h3 id="generate-multi-factor-authentication-mfa-recovery-codes-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|object|false|none|
|» count|body|number|false|The number of recovery codes to generate. Must be between 1 and 50. Defaults to the provider's configured value when omitted.|

> Example responses

> 400 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Discount must be set to dynamic",
  "type": "not_allowed"
}
```

> 404 Response

```json
{
  "message": "Entity with id 1 was not found",
  "type": "not_found"
}
```

> 409 Response

```json
{

}
```

> 422 Response

```json
{
  "code": "invalid_request_error",
  "message": "Discount with code TEST already exists.",
  "type": "duplicate_error"
}
```

> 500 Response

```json
{
  "code": "api_error",
  "message": "An error occured while hashing password",
  "type": "database_error"
}
```

<h1 id="medusa-storefront-api-orders">Orders</h1>

Guest and registered customers can view orders they placed.

These API routes allow customers to view their orders.


## List Logged-in Customer's Orders

<a id="opIdGetOrders"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/store/orders \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'x-publishable-api-key: string' \
  -H "Cookie: connect.sid=${API_KEY}"
```

`GET /store/orders`

Retrieve the orders of the logged-in customer. The orders can be filtered by fields such as `id`. The orders can also be sorted or paginated.

<h3 id="list-logged-in-customers-orders-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|x-publishable-api-key|header|string|true|Publishable API Key created in the Medusa Admin.|
|x-medusa-locale|header|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|fields|query|string|false|Comma-separated fields that should be included in the returned data. if a field is prefixed with `+` it will be added to the default fields, using `-` will remove it from the default fields. without prefix it will replace the entire default fields.|
|offset|query|number|false|The number of items to skip when retrieving a list.|
|limit|query|number|false|Limit the number of items returned in the list.|
|order|query|string|false|The field to sort the data by. By default, the sort order is ascending. To change the order to descending, prefix the field name with `-`.|
|id|query|string \| [string]|false|none|
|$and|query|[object]|false|none|
|$or|query|[object]|false|none|
|status|query|string \| [string]|false|none|
|with_deleted|query|boolean|false|Whether to include deleted records in the result.|
|locale|query|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|

<h3 id="list-logged-in-customers-orders-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|Inline|
|400|Bad Request|Client Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|401|Unauthorized|User is not authorized. Must log in first|Inline|
|404|Not Found|Not Found Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|409|Conflict|Invalid State Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|422|Unprocessable Entity|Invalid Request Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|
|500|Internal Server Error|Server Error|[Error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="list-logged-in-customers-orders-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|number|true|none|The maximum number of items returned.|
|offset|number|true|none|The number of items skipped before retrieving the returned items.|
|count|number|true|none|The total number of items.|
|orders|[[StoreOrder](#schemastoreorder)]|true|none|The order's orders.|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
cookie_auth, jwt_token
</aside>

## Get an Order

<a id="opIdGetOrdersId"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/store/orders/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'x-publishable-api-key: string'
```

`GET /store/orders/{id}`

Retrieve an order by its ID. You can expand the order's relations or select the fields that should be returned. This API route doesn't require customer authentication, so that guest customers can view their order confirmation page after placing an order. To restrict access to this API route, refer to the [Restrict Order Retrieval guide](https://docs.medusajs.com/resources/commerce-modules/order/secure-order-retrieval).

<h3 id="get-an-order-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The order's ID.|
|x-publishable-api-key|header|string|true|Publishable API Key created in the Medusa Admin.|
|x-medusa-locale|header|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|fields|query|string|false|Comma-separated fields that should be included in the returned data. if a field is prefixed with `+` it will be added to the default fields, using `-` will remove it from the default fields. without prefix it will replace the entire default fields.|
|locale|query|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|

</aside>

## Accept Order Transfer

<a id="opIdPostOrdersIdTransferAccept"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:9000/store/orders/string/transfer/accept \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H 'x-publishable-api-key: string' \
  -d '{
    "token": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /store/orders/{id}/transfer/accept`

Accept an order to be transfered to a customer's account, which was specified when the transfer request was created. The transfer is requested previously either by the customer using the [Request Order Transfer Store API route](https://docs.medusajs.com/api/store#orders_postordersidtransferrequest), or by the admin using the [Request Order Transfer Admin API route](https://docs.medusajs.com/api/admin#orders_postordersidtransferrequest).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "token": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="accept-order-transfer-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|The order's ID.|
|x-publishable-api-key|header|string|true|Publishable API Key created in the Medusa Admin.|
|x-medusa-locale|header|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|fields|query|string|false|Comma-separated fields that should be included in the returned data.<br>if a field is prefixed with `+` it will be added to the default fields, using `-` will remove it from the default fields.<br>without prefix it will replace the entire default fields.|
|locale|query|string|false|The locale in BCP 47 format to retrieve localized content.|
|body|body|[StoreAcceptOrderTransfer](#schemastoreacceptordertransfer)|false|none|
|» token|body|string|true|The order transfer's token issued when the transfer was requested.|
